reason: Ghosts, sleepers and household pests establish a strong haunted-house roster, with one repeated baby weakening its final discovery slot.
recommendation: Replace the repeated Mime Jr. slot with Mismagius; keep Mime Jr. on Route116 and retain Sinistea, Shuppet and Sableye.

reason: Pollinators, flower Fairies and the striking Pheromosa discovery form a coherent meadow with immediate team-building value.
Mantyke on the Old Rod and shoreline rock residents give the harbor character, but its Super Rod pool barely emphasizes that signature family.
recommendation: Swap Mantine and Clawitzer Super Rod positions so Mantine becomes 30% and Clawitzer 10%; preserve Mantyke at 40% on the Old Rod.

reason: Makuhita, Aron and Abra provide useful cave discoveries, though repeated Timburr dilutes the entrance habitat after its Route102 addition.
recommendation: Replace the repeated Timburr slot with another Aron slot, making Aron 18%; keep Timburr on Route102 and the lower cave floor.

reason: Mawile, Sableye and Bronzor suit the deeper cave, but several entrance-floor repeats keep its residents from standing out.
recommendation: Replace repeated Timburr and Glimmet slots with additional Mawile and Sableye slots, raising those residents to 16% and 15% while retaining both displaced species elsewhere.

reason: Tinkatink, Duraludon and Deino provide strong deeper discoveries, while the common Aron slot repeats the entrance more than necessary.
recommendation: Replace the repeated Aron slot with another Tinkatink slot, making Tinkatink 17%; retain Aron on 1F and B1F and keep Duraludon and Deino.

reason: Beldum, Metang and Lucario reward reaching Steven, but generic cave residents occupy most of their apparent signature room.
recommendation: Replace the repeated Aron and Sableye slots with Beldum and Metang, making those 21% and 17%; retain Lucario and the other mineral residents.

reason: The city ponds begin with Marill and Lombre but their later methods become a largely marine roster disconnected from the setting.
recommendation: Keep Old Rod Marill; use Marill/Lombre/Poliwhirl/Shellos/Bibarel for Surf, Goldeen/Corphish/Wooper for Good Rod, and Azumarill/Ludicolo/Crawdaunt/Quagsire/Dratini for Super Rod.

reason: Fast bugs, mushroom support, early Pichu and durable Ferroseed combine practical opening roles with clear woodland and tree residents.
Caterpie, Weedle, Kakuna and Metapod take 46% of encounters, making the second forest feel less rewarding than its monkeys and rarer bugs suggest.
recommendation: Replace the repeated Caterpie 13% slot with Heracross 13% for a substantial new forest catch; retain Caterpie in the first woods, the unique cocoons, the three monkeys and Larvesta.

reason: Kartana, dark woodland residents and swamp insects create a memorable deeper forest, but several rod catches feel imported from coastal pools.
recommendation: Keep Kartana and every land discovery; replace Super Rod Lanturn and Octillery with Araquanid and Gastrodon to extend the local Dewpider/Shellos habitat.

reason: Mienfoo, Guts Taillow, quick Wurmple evolution and flexible Eevee/Bonsly preparation now make the first route useful immediately without losing its familiar residents.
Timburr and Pachirisu complement its babies and pond species exceptionally well, while Octillery and Sharpedo weaken the later freshwater identity.
recommendation: Keep every opening land slot; replace Good Rod Octillery with Buizel and Super Rod Sharpedo with Bibarel.

reason: Shellos, Growlithe and the Electric choices help the first rival, but later fishing undersells the creek’s own water family.
recommendation: Keep every early land catch and replace Super Rod Wishiwashi with Gastrodon to give returning players a local evolution payoff.

reason: Azurill and Budew remain worthwhile, but five overlapping bird families leave too many similar low-cap catches between the new opening teams and the forest.
recommendation: Replace Pidgey and Pidove with Fletchinder and Roselia for immediate distinct roles; relocate the two displaced birds into repeated bird slots on later routes, preserving all babies here.

reason: Its palm-shore land roster and large marine Surf residents fit well, but Luvdisc dominates the strongest rod without a special reason to return.
recommendation: Replace the 30% Super Rod Luvdisc slot with Octillery and the 25% Bruxish slot with Cloyster, retaining the other rocky-shore catches.

reason: The Fighting beach, Hawlucha and Falinks offer a distinct practical identity beside Granite Cave, with one poorly matched rock encounter.
recommendation: Replace Rock Smash Woobat with Shuckle; preserve Woobat in its cave habitats and retain every Fighting option.

reason: The strait has a useful variety of fish but little separates its later rod discoveries from neighboring sea routes.
recommendation: Make the Arrokuda line its signature: replace Good Rod Octillery with Barraskewda and swap Barraskewda/Qwilfish Super Rod positions to give Barraskewda 30%.

reason: Frillish, Dragalge and the localized Dhelmise discovery make the waters around the wreck recognizably different from ordinary coastlines.
Sandygast and Pincurchin make the beach rocks rewarding, but later fishing mostly repeats surrounding coastlines.
recommendation: Replace Good Rod Octillery with Krabby and Super Rod Staryu with Pincurchin, emphasizing the beach residents while preserving Sandygast in the rocks.

reason: Electric species and pollution-adapted residents clearly express the urban road, although Electrike repeats earlier access without adding a new role.
recommendation: Replace the repeated Electrike slot with Toxtricity as a ready urban Poison/Electric discovery; retain Electrike on Route103 and every unique urban species here.

reason: Desert plants, sand specialists, Galarian Yamask and Stonjourner contrast cleanly with the freshwater oasis and rocky encounters.
Xatu, the Rockruff forms and Sandy Shocks establish a distinctive ruin habitat, with repeated Hawlucha adding less identity than the local psychic residents.
recommendation: Replace the repeated Hawlucha slot with another Xatu slot, making Xatu 21%; retain Hawlucha on Route106/112, both Rockruff forms and Sandy Shocks.

reason: Volcanic residents and a varied Fighting group suit the mountain approach, but repeated Mienfoo contributes little new discovery.
recommendation: Replace the repeated Mienfoo slot with another Numel slot, raising Numel to 18%; keep Mienfoo on Route101 and all other Fighting choices.

reason: Spinda, Skarmory, Spoink and Slugma establish the ashland identity, while repeated Mienfoo is less distinctive than those residents.
recommendation: Replace the repeated Mienfoo slot with another Skarmory slot, raising Skarmory to 19%; preserve Mienfoo earlier and all unique ashland finds.

reason: Swablu, Zangoose/Seviper, foothill mammals and a coherent freshwater roster give this route both strong identity and useful discoveries.
The coastal meadow has good Fairy and Fighting finds, but its Super Rod lineup is almost the same generic marine group used elsewhere.
recommendation: Keep the land roster and give Super Rod a rocky-coast pool of Barbaracle, Kingler, Cloyster, Mantine and Wishiwashi.

reason: Mime Jr., Munchlax, Riolu and Throh give practical pre-gym tools alongside early birds, insects and a Dreepy investment.
Daycare mammals, flowers and the unusual Old Rod pair create a strong meadow, with Octillery the main freshwater mismatch.
recommendation: Replace Good Rod Octillery with Poliwag; retain Ditto, Audino, both Old Rod discoveries and the flower-associated rock encounters.

reason: Ready evolved partners and unusual land discoveries support the eastward transition, but repeated Duraludon weakens this route’s own field identity.
recommendation: Replace the repeated Duraludon slot with another Passimian slot, raising Passimian to 15%; retain Duraludon in Granite Cave and other established locations.

reason: Rainforest residents, mushroom support, Feebas and Raging Bolt make this a distinctive and rewarding major habitat.
Pumpkaboo sizes and eerie woodland finds give strong land identity, but Tropius and the familiar river pool repeat neighboring routes.
recommendation: Replace repeated Tropius with Trevenant; distinguish its water with Wooper/Quagsire/Politoed/Masquerain/Corphish and retain every Pumpkaboo size.

reason: Mimikyu, Poltchageist and darker evolved residents suit the approach to Mt. Pyre, but generic rod catches understate the haunted waters.
recommendation: Replace Super Rod Octillery and Golduck with Frillish and Jellicent to emphasize the existing ghost-water family.

reason: Frillish and rare Dhelmise fit Mt. Pyre’s waters, while the more common rod catches still resemble ordinary offshore fishing.
recommendation: Replace Good Rod Octillery with Frillish and Super Rod Clawitzer with Jellicent; preserve the 10% Dhelmise discovery.

reason: The berry-route bugs and plant families are promising, but common Mightyena/Linoone and late Patrat make the land roster feel like leftover placements.
recommendation: Replace repeated Mightyena and Linoone slots with additional Applin and Smoliv slots; move Patrat to Route117’s duplicate Exeggcute slot and use its Route123 slot for another Shelmet.

reason: Whismur, Chingling, useful Fighting/Ground partners and long-term dragons give the first tunnel a clear acoustic cave identity and practical breadth.
Damp cave animals and both Stunfisk forms make sense on land, while Wailord and the generic fishing pools do little to express an enclosed tidal cave.
recommendation: Replace Surf Wailord with Chinchou, Good Rod Luvdisc with Chinchou, and Super Rod Bruxish with Lanturn; retain both Stunfisk forms and the rocky cave catches.

reason: A dedicated Ice chamber with Smoochum, Cryogonal and Frigibax offers a clear habitat and several useful kinds of discovery.
White flowers, Psychic/Fairy support and Iron Leaves create a distinct second meadow without simply repeating Dewford’s pollinators.
